learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding: Knowledge and understanding of mathematics and other basic sciences inherent to their engineering specialty, at a level that allows them to acquire the rest of the degree's competencies.

Engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods appropriately, and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Engineering projects: Ability to project, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems of their specialty, that comply with established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes, and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Ability to apply engineering practice standards in their specialty.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.

Communicates, searches, and correctly structures information orally: Delivers a clear and concise oral presentation and defense of the project, adequately using the aspects included in the oral communication guide and computer tools.
Uses the appropriate methodology to find solutions to problems and to develop projects: Examines problems well, searches for significant information to address them, and proposes solutions.
Limits and defines the necessary tolerances for the parts that form a mechanical assembly respecting technical drawing standards.

Communicates, searches, and correctly structures information in writing: Drafts a clear and concise project report following the criteria established in the project report writing guide and using the computer tool.
Represents different types of parts respecting technical drawing standards.
Shows group work skills and solves problems using the most appropriate tools in each case.

teaching_methods: Development, drafting, and presentation of reports, memos, audiovisual material, etc. related to projects/POPBLs, carried out individually or in teams
Individual study and work, quizzes, exams, and/or control points
Completion of exercises individually and in teams
Teacher presentation in the classroom, in participatory classes, of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects

assessment_methods.method: Technical ability, involvement in the project/PBL, work done, results obtained, documentation submitted, technical presentation and defense
Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Reports on exercise completion, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices

assessment_rules: For some learning outcomes (RGM182, RGM191, RGM181, RGM192), there are no recovery mechanisms. For other outcomes (RGM142, RGM141), individual written and oral tests can be recovered. Control points for continuous learning outcomes have no recovery. A recovery control point performed at the end of the semester will have a weight of 75%. All assignments must be submitted to be eligible for control points. If all assignments are not submitted, their respective grades will not be taken into account. In case of plagiarism or being copied, the corresponding assignment grades will not be taken into account.
